subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Stirling Cycle: Heat From Outside
description: A quick, practical guide to The Stirling Cycle: Heat From Outside.

hook.text: A Stirling engine runs on any heat source — flame, sunlight, even the warmth of your hand.

buildup.text: Heat is applied externally. A sealed gas inside expands and contracts between hot and cold zones.

discovery.text: A regenerator stores heat between cycles, boosting efficiency. The same gas is reused over and over — no exhaust.

twist.text: Stirling engines are quiet and clean. But they respond slowly to load changes. That limits their use in cars.

climax.text: Submarines use Stirling engines for silent running. Solar dishes use them to convert focused sunlight to electricity.

punchline.text: Any heat source. No exhaust. The quietest engine you'll never hear.

quiz.question: Why aren't Stirling engines widely used in cars?
options: They can only run on solar energy and not on liquid fuels
They respond slowly to changes in power demand
Their internal gas leaks out and must be constantly replaced
